headline: Los Angeles writes its name by hand, in Chicano letters.
summary: LA's public art runs in a Chicano line, from Siqueiros' 1932 América Tropical on Olvera Street to Self Help Graphics' screenprints in Boyle Heights. Its type is Eastside: cholo calligraphy, Old English and hand-painted rótulos. For Lakers fans, though, the walls belong to Kobe. Both new uniforms look backward, so nobody has drawn Doncic, Reaves or Kessler yet. Commission that look from LA's own artists.

insights.title: Kobe owns the walls
insights.detail: Since Jan 26, 2020, LA muralists have painted hundreds of Kobe and Gianna walls, from Boyle Heights to the Valley. Aug 24 has been the city's official Kobe Bryant Day since 2016, and the Feb 2024 Kobe statue made Star Plaza a pilgrimage site.
insights.implication: Nike holds the Kobe line, so estate-approved 8/24 product made with the muralists who painted those walls is the most emotionally credible thing Nike can sell in LA. Make it about his craft and his life, never the crash.

insights.title: LA's mural tradition is Chicano
insights.detail: The city's public-art canon runs from Siqueiros' América Tropical (1932, Olvera Street) to the 1970s murals of Estrada Courts. It includes Judy Baca and SPARC's half-mile Great Wall (1976-84) and the serigraph ateliers at Self Help Graphics in Boyle Heights.
insights.implication: Product for the Lakers' large Latino fan base should come out of this lineage. Pay and credit SHG or SPARC artists, use real screenprint craft, and skip off-the-shelf papel picado and sugar-skull templates.

insights.title: Lettering is the city's signature
insights.detail: Chaz Bojórquez took cholo placas into museums as calligraphy. Mister Cartoon and Estevan Oriol carried Old English and black-and-gray tattoo lettering from the Eastside to Nike, Joker Brand and album covers. Mark Bradford built his abstractions from South LA merchant posters.
insights.implication: Commission an original "Los Angeles" and "Lakers" alphabet from a credited Chicano letterer, not stock blackletter. Custom type is the fastest way to make product read as LA-made.

insights.title: The transit map is already purple and gold
insights.detail: Metro's D Line runs purple under Wilshire through Koreatown, with a station at Wilshire/Western beneath the Wiltern. The E Line runs gold from Santa Monica past Pico station at the arena, then through Little Tokyo and Mariachi Plaza in Boyle Heights to East LA. Together they trace the Lakers' footprint.
insights.implication: A licensed route-map and station-typography capsule says purple and gold the way only LA can. It also ties Koreatown, Downtown and the Eastside into one story.

insights.title: Showtime's home is Clippers property
insights.detail: Jack Kent Cooke's Forum (1967) was Charles Luckman's colonnaded drum, where purple was renamed "Forum Blue" and Showtime played out. Steve Ballmer bought it in 2020. It is now the Kia Forum, a Clippers-owned ground in Inglewood next door to the Intuit Dome.
insights.implication: Tell the Showtime story through cues the Lakers own, such as gold numerals and Sunday Whites. Add the Forum Blue color story once the mark is cleared. Build the "home" imagery downtown around Star Plaza, not the Forum building.

insights.title: The Luka era has no visual canon yet
insights.detail: LeBron has left for Philadelphia, and none of last season's top five playoff-minutes players returned. Both new uniforms look backward: the revived 2023-24 triangle-wordmark City Edition and Nike's Specter for historic franchises. LA's walls have not yet drawn Doncic, Reaves and Kessler.
insights.implication: Commission the new era's walls and lifestyle graphics from LA artists now, before bootleggers and fan accounts define it. Coordinate any Luka imagery with Jordan Brand.

places.name: Self Help Graphics & Art
places.why: Its serigraph atelier and Día de los Muertos celebration have driven Chicano graphic art since the early 1970s. That makes it the natural partner for Latino-fandom product.

places.name: Estrada Courts
places.why: Dozens of murals painted since the early 1970s make it one of the Eastside's densest and most respected outdoor galleries.

places.name: The Great Wall of Los Angeles
places.neighborhood: Valley Glen (Tujunga Wash, Coldwater Canyon Ave)
places.why: Judy Baca and SPARC's half-mile mural of California history, painted 1976-84 with hundreds of young people, anchors the Valley's public art.

places.name: Star Plaza at Crypto.com Arena
places.why: Bronzes of Magic, Kareem, Jerry West, Shaq, Elgin Baylor, Chick Hearn and Kobe (2024) make the arena's front door the Lakers' outdoor hall of fame.

places.name: Broadway Theatre District
places.why: A dozen 1910s-30s movie palaces, among them the Los Angeles, Orpheum, Million Dollar and Palace, give LA its richest stretch of blade signs, marquees and display lettering.

places.name: The Wiltern
places.why: The 1931 blue-green terra-cotta tower above the D Line station anchors Koreatown's Hangul-neon corridor along Wilshire.

places.name: Watts Towers and Watts Towers Arts Center
places.why: Simon Rodia's 17 towers, built 1921-54 of steel and mortar and encrusted with broken tile, bottle glass and shells, are South LA's monument to found-object craft.

places.name: Art + Practice
places.why: Mark Bradford's exhibition and community space sits at the center of Black LA's arts village. It is a credible door into Black Lakers fandom.

places.name: ArtCenter College of Design
places.why: LA's leading product, transportation and illustration school, and a long-standing pipeline into footwear and apparel design.

places.name: Venice Art Walls
places.why: The Westside's public stage for LA writers' hand-styles. It is repainted constantly, so it shows where lettering is heading.

people.name: Judith F. Baca
people.role: Muralist, SPARC founder, UCLA professor emerita
people.why: Her Great Wall set LA's model of community-painted history. That makes SPARC the right partner for any Lakers history mural.

people.name: Chaz Bojórquez
people.why: He took Eastside cholo lettering into museums, starting with his "Señor Suerte" skull in 1969. He is the authority to draw an original LA alphabet.

people.name: Mister Cartoon
people.role: Tattoo, lettering and lowrider artist (SA Studios)
people.why: LA's best-known black-and-gray and Old English artist has designed sneakers with Nike and co-founded Joker Brand with Estevan Oriol.

people.name: Estevan Oriol
people.why: His "LA Fingers" photograph is the city's hand-sign image. Decades shooting lowriders, tattoo and hip-hop make him a ready campaign lens.

people.name: Andrew D. Bernstein
people.why: He has shot the Lakers since the Showtime era and photographed Kobe's whole career, including the images in "The Mamba Mentality." His archive is the franchise's visual memory.

people.name: Gustavo Zermeño Jr.
people.why: He painted several of the most-shared Kobe and Gianna murals after 2020, so he has already shown he can paint what Lakers fans feel.

people.name: Gajin Fujita
people.why: Raised in Boyle Heights, he layers Edo woodblock imagery and gold leaf with LA graffiti lettering. That blend of Japanese American and Eastside culture is found only in LA.

people.name: Mark Bradford
people.why: One of LA's most celebrated artists, he built his work from South LA merchant posters and hair-salon end papers, and rooted his foundation in Leimert Park.

moments.name: Lakers home opener vs Golden State
moments.why: The first home night of the full Luka era is the launch date for a Metro purple-and-gold capsule and any reveal of the new era's murals.

moments.name: Día de los Muertos at Self Help Graphics
moments.why: Boyle Heights' printmaking-centered celebration, held since the early 1970s, is where to meet and support Eastside artists. Don't brand the altars.

moments.name: Christmas Day vs Philadelphia
moments.why: LeBron James' first game back in LA will show whether fans honor or paint over his LA walls.

moments.name: LA Art Show
moments.timing: Winter, at the LA Convention Center (recent editions late Jan to mid-Feb)
moments.why: A large art fair next door to Crypto.com Arena, ready-made for an artist-collab pop-up that shares foot traffic with a Lakers home stand.

moments.name: Frieze Los Angeles
moments.timing: Late February, Santa Monica Airport, with satellite fairs such as Felix at the Hollywood Roosevelt
moments.why: The week the international art world comes to LA is the high-culture stage for a Lakers artist commission.

moments.name: Jacaranda season
moments.why: Purple blooms carpet LA streets just as the playoffs run, a natural, non-licensed purple moment.

moments.name: Kobe Day (8/24)
moments.why: The city-declared Kobe Bryant Day, when fans visit the murals and Star Plaza, is the release date for Kobe-line product made with LA muralists.

moments.name: Watts Towers Day of the Drum and Jazz festivals
moments.why: Long-running South LA festivals at the towers, and a way to engage Watts before the season starts.

vocabulary.meaning: Jack Kent Cooke's name for Lakers purple after the team moved into his Forum in 1967. Old-school fans still use it.
The Lakers' white-and-gold home uniforms, traditionally worn for Sunday and holiday home games.
Kobe's two jersey numbers, shorthand for him and his mindset, and Aug 24, the city's Kobe Bryant Day.
Chicano graffiti name-tags and roll calls written in cholo hand-style. They are the root of LA's lettering and are often tied to a specific neighborhood or gang.
Hand-painted Spanish-language storefront signs on panaderías, carnicerías and llanteras across the Eastside and South LA.
The fine-line, single-needle tattoo style born in East LA and California prisons in the 1970s. It is now global but still rooted in Chicano LA.
1950s-60s stucco box apartments over open carports, decorated with starbursts and script names like "The Capri." They are all over LA.
Space-age coffee-shop architecture named for John Lautner's 1949 Googies on Sunset. Pann's and Norms La Cienega are the living examples.

designCues.cue: Lakers purple #552583 under its Showtime name, "Forum Blue," paired with Lakers gold #FDB927.
designCues.source: Jack Kent Cooke renamed purple 'Forum Blue' when the Lakers moved into his Forum in 1967.
designCues.use: Use it as the colorway name and hang-tag story on Showtime-heritage pieces, after clearing the "Forum" mark with the Kia Forum's owners.

designCues.cue: Jacaranda blue-violet (approx. #8F7BC9), lighter, bluer and softer than Lakers purple.
designCues.source: LA's street jacarandas bloom in May and June, carpeting sidewalks from the Valley to South LA during the playoffs.
designCues.use: A second purple for playoff and lifestyle tonal packs, such as a Forum Blue-to-jacaranda gradient. At most a petal-scatter print, never literal flower clip art.

designCues.cue: A custom "Los Angeles"/"Lakers" alphabet in Chicano hand-style: tall, compressed, sharp-serifed letters with Old English blackletter capitals.
designCues.source: Cholo placas and calligraphy from Chaz Bojórquez, Old English tattoo lettering from Mister Cartoon, and Eastside rótulos.
designCues.use: Commission and credit a working Eastside letterer for chest scripts, neck tape and tee graphics. Never reproduce real placas, neighborhood names or gang numerals.

designCues.cue: Vertically stacked capitals in outlined neon-tube strokes over a marquee field of chaser bulbs, plus Hangul neon after dark.
designCues.source: Broadway's movie-palace blade signs (Los Angeles, Orpheum, Million Dollar) and Koreatown's signage along Wilshire, Western and 6th Street.
designCues.use: Run "LOS ANGELES" or a player name down a side seam or sleeve. For a Koreatown piece, have a Korean American designer set the Hangul (레이커스) rather than machine-translating it.

designCues.cue: Deep candy purple and gold metalflake with hand-pulled pinstripe scrolls and gold-leaf accents.
designCues.source: Eastside lowrider culture on Whittier Boulevard and LA's kustom pinstriping tradition.
designCues.use: Use metallic-flake heat transfers on numbers, iridescent shooting-shirt fabric and pinstripe trims drawn by a working lowrider pinstriper. Credit the pinstriper on the hang tag.

designCues.cue: Irregular broken-tile, bottle-glass and seashell mosaic set in gray mortar.
designCues.use: An all-over sublimated or jacquard pattern for shorts panels or warmups, developed with and benefiting the Watts Towers Arts Center. Don't use a photo of the towers.

designCues.cue: Day-glo letterpress posters with a split-fountain gradient (hot pink #FF2E93 into fluorescent yellow #FFE600) and fat wood-type capitals.
designCues.source: LA's Colby Poster Printing Co., whose posters advertised boxing cards, swap meets, dances and concerts across Southern California for decades.
designCues.use: Use it for game-night posters, tees and rivalry-game graphics printed by an LA screenprinter or letterpress shop.

designCues.cue: Three serrated stripes in olive green, orange gold and vineyard red, divided by zigzag edges.
designCues.source: The 1931 City of Los Angeles flag, whose colors stand for the olive, the orange and the grape.
designCues.use: A sawtooth trim at hems, cuffs or waistbands in Lakers gold with green and red accents. Use the stripes, never the city seal.

productHooks: "8/24 Wall Series" for Kobe Day: three LA muralists who painted Kobe walls each design one Nike Kobe-line tee or hoodie. Each piece is estate-approved and credited on the jock tag. It releases Aug 24 and sends proceeds to the Mamba & Mambacita Sports Foundation.

"Purple Line / Gold Line" opening-night capsule (Oct 21 vs Golden State). Route-map graphics trace the D Line through Koreatown and the E Line from Santa Monica to East LA, past Pico station, in Metro-style station type. License it from Metro and sell it at L.A. Live.

"Eastside Serigraph" Latino-fandom capsule made in Self Help Graphics' atelier: hand-pulled screenprint tees and posters with a custom "Los Angeles" alphabet by a credited Chicano letterer. Launch it at the Lakers' Latino heritage night, with proceeds to SHG.
"Jacaranda" playoff pack: a Forum Blue-to-jacaranda tonal shooting shirt and lifestyle fleece. It drops in May as the blooms peak, during the West semifinal stretch where the 2026 run ended.

"1960" lifestyle line for the City Edition revival: pair the Minneapolis-move triangle wordmark with the LA the team arrived in. Draw on dingbat-apartment script, Googie starbursts and the LA Memorial Sports Arena, the Lakers' first LA home (1960-67).

"First Walls" for the Luka era: fund new murals in five footprint neighborhoods (Boyle Heights, Koreatown, Leimert Park, the Valley and Venice). Release each one as a numbered, artist-credited tee. Coordinate any Luka imagery with Jordan Brand.
watchouts: Kobe imagery needs the Bryant estate's approval. Keep helicopter, crash-date and angel-wing imagery off product, along with any Gianna imagery the family hasn't signed off. Every Kobe mural is its painter's copyright under VARA and California's Art Preservation Act, so license it, including photographs of the walls.

Cholo lettering, placas, certain numerals and color pairings can signal gang affiliation, so work only through credited Chicano letterers. Keep Día de los Muertos altars and calaveras and the Virgen de Guadalupe off product. They are spiritual and sacred imagery, not decoration.

Boyle Heights' anti-gentrification "artwashing" protests pushed several galleries out in 2017-18. Let Eastside organizations lead any event there, and make sure it benefits them. No brand pop-up that "discovers" the Eastside.

Third-party IP needs clearance: the Hollywood Sign and Walk of Fame (Hollywood Chamber of Commerce), LA Metro marks and route graphics, the Wiltern and the LA city seal. The Kia Forum name and building belong to Ballmer's company.

LeBron is a lifetime Nike athlete, so Christmas Day product around his return with the 76ers should honor his 2020 title era, not mock him. After the January 2025 Palisades and Eaton fires, keep flame, ash and "LA burning" graphics off product.
